checkpoints.description: [1/5] Plan: add advisory detection of used types whose defining internal header is not reachable from the translation unit, reusing the pure identifier scanner and path query.

impact_assessment.why: A very common C++ error is using a type whose header was never included (or was only included transitively elsewhere); compilers report it far from the cause.
impact_assessment.benefits: Actionable 'consider including X.hpp' advice derived from the same inspectable graph, with no compiler or third-party tooling.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new recommendation kind and render label; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the analysis stays pure and uses the existing path query.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Advisory-only wording, restrict candidates to scanned headers and exact type identifiers, golden tests for included vs missing cases, full gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [2/5] Pure core: missing_includes reuses identifier scanner and path query; add-include kind in renderers and snapshots; 164 checks green.
[3/5] Shell: no new I/O path; advisory surfaced through the existing scan renderer; fixture smoke confirms add-include appears only when the header is unreachable.
[4/5] README, ADR-006, map and consolidated audit updated; 5/5 gates pass and 164 checks green.
Task 'knot-missing-includes' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add knot init to write starter .knotignore and .knot-policy, keeping content generation pure and file writes at the edge.

impact_assessment.why: A new user has to discover the policy and ignore file syntax before getting value; zero-friction onboarding is part of the architectural brief.
impact_assessment.benefits: One command produces a documented starting point that the user can edit; content is generated by a pure function so it is testable without touching disk.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: two generated files and --force semantics; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: generation is pure, writes guarded so existing files are never overwritten silently.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Golden content tests, refusal on existing files without --force, smoke in a temp directory, full gate run before commit.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Pure core: default_ignore_text/default_policy_text generators; 168 checks green.
[3/4] Shell: knot init with --force guard, write at the edge; overwrite refusal and forced write verified in a temp directory.
[4/4] README, ADR-007, map and consolidated audit updated; 5/5 gates pass and 168 checks green.
Task 'knot-init-scaffold' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add knot baseline <dir> <file> [--force] that writes a complete JSON snapshot from a pure renderer, with an overwrite guard at the I/O edge.

impact_assessment.why: Regressions are only useful if a reviewed state can be promoted to the new baseline; requiring manual shell redirection invites truncated or stale baselines.
impact_assessment.benefits: A complete, deterministic baseline in one command, protected from accidental overwrite, with the same round-trip guarantees as scan --format json.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a new subcommand and complete-snapshot renderer; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: generation stays pure, write guarded.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure render_baseline_json with a round-trip test that every node is captured; refuse overwrite without --force; smoke on a fixture; full gates before commit.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Pure core: render_baseline_json complete snapshot; round-trip test over a 16-node graph; 174 checks green.
[3/4] Shell: knot baseline with overwrite guard; smoke shows exit 0/2 and a clean diff against the written file.
[4/4] README, ADR-008, map and consolidated audit updated; 5/5 gates pass and 174 checks green.
Task 'knot-baseline-lifecycle' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Plan: add knot stats with file/edge classification and a deterministic deepest include chain, computed by a pure bounded BFS over the graph.

impact_assessment.why: Cost per file tells you how much a single file pulls in, but a project-level view of depth and internal/external coupling is what maintainers track over time.
impact_assessment.benefits: A compact, reproducible metrics surface suitable for dashboards and CI logs, with no new dependency or I/O path.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new subcommand and stats schema; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: depth search must be bounded and deterministic.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the existing pure shortest_path BFS per node with a step guard, tie-break by lexicographic chain, golden tests for a known graph, full gates before commit.
